newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks fall in quiet, bluechip trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks fall in quiet, bluechip trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell 0.18 percent on Wednesday in the quietest turnover for nearly three weeks, focused on a handful of banks, cement and phosphate firms.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.29 points to end the week at 159.47 points in turnover worth just 707,000 ($1 million).
Turnover last week, boosted by foreign fund purchasing, averaged around 3.3 million dinars daily.
"It's a little slow, but it's stable," said analyst Mohammad Abdullah. "There is still selective demand." The index has hovered around 159.5 to 159.7 points all week.
Wednesday's trade centred on Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturers, which rose 0.06 dinars to 3.91 dinars in turnover worth nearly 95,000 dinars.
Arab Bank fell 1.50 dinars to 254.00 dinars after shares worth nearly 87,000 changed hands and Jordan Phosphate Mines ended unchanged on 4.00 dinars after business worth around 84,000 dinars.
The stocks are expected to be the targets of international investors if foreign buying picks up again.
Overall 15 shares rose on Wednesday and 13 fell, with another 20 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.09 percent to 81.04 points, 2.82 percent down from the start of the year.
